findings.explanation: resolvePageCredential decrypts the page's Facebook access token and immediately writes the raw plaintext secret to stdout on every successful lookup (i.e. on every inbound webhook/admin call that needs to send a message). This directly violates the project's own documented rule in .agent/skills/credential-safety.md ('A token is received once and never echoed back. Never print, log, return, snapshot, or test against a real token.'). Anyone with access to application logs (Railway log viewer, log aggregator, error tracker breadcrumbs) can read a live, usable Facebook Page access token for the shop, allowing them to send messages as the page or make other Graph API calls with it. There is no redact/mask call on this line (compare to pageRef()/redactSensitiveText() used consistently elsewhere in core/webhook.js). Fix: delete the line or replace with a safe summary like `console.log(`[credentials] resolved token for shop=${shopRef(normalizedShopId)}`)`.
